topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.

papers.title: Isoflurane anesthesia CNS recovery state: ultra-slow oscillations and cellular-stress-responsive gene expression
papers.abstract: General anesthesia and NREM sleep share slow-wave EEG features, yet whether anesthesia substitutes for physiological sleep remains unclear. We compared recovery from 4h of isoflurane anesthesia (IA) with time-matched sleep and sleep deprivation (SD) in male C57BL/6J mice using continuous EEG/EMG recordings and frontal cortex RNA sequencing. IA recovery produced transient, rebound arousal, reduced early NREM and REM sleep, and, fragmented subsequent NREM bouts, and persistant, ultra-slow EEG-oscillations that normalized within two weeks. Whereas, SD induced consolidated rebound sleep and slow wave activity. Transcriptomic profiling at ZT6 showed that IA and SD induced largely distinct cortical gene-expression programs. IA preferentially enriched integrated stress response and unfolded protein response genes, whereas SD showed a comparatively orthogonal, growth-permissive, mTOR-associated profile. Although IA-induced gene-expression suggests cellular stress, corticosterone measurements argued against systemic stress as the primary driver. These findings indicate that isoflurane recovery is neurophysiologically and molecularly distinct from restorative sleep.

ai.reason: Directly relevant animal sleep/anesthesia study with continuous EEG/EMG, ultra-slow oscillations, and recovery dynamics; highly transferable to the researcher's animal sleep experiments.
ai.summary: Compared recovery from 4 h isoflurane anesthesia with time-matched sleep and sleep deprivation in mice using EEG/EMG and frontal cortex RNA sequencing; isoflurane recovery produced transient rebound arousal, fragmented NREM, and persistent ultra-slow oscillations normalizing within two weeks, with cortical transcriptomics distinct from sleep deprivation (integrated stress response/unfolded protein response enrichment vs. growth-permissive mTOR-associated profile).

papers.title: Multi-parametric spectral modeling disentangles synaptic kinetics and neural excitability from non-invasive electrophysiological recordings
papers.abstract: Spectral modeling of electrophysiological recordings enables non-invasive characterization of neural excitability. However, current approaches rely on a single spectral index, limiting insight into the multiple biophysical processes underlying excitation-inhibition balance. Here, we introduce a biologically informed, multi-parametric spectral analysis that disentangles neural excitability and synaptic kinetics from recordings. As a proof of concept, we demonstrate that this approach captures signatures of hyperexcitability and glutamate reuptake dysfunction characteristic of Alzheimer's disease.

ai.reason: Directly provides an interpretable, biologically informed spectral decomposition method for non-invasive electrophysiology, highly relevant to the researcher's spectral modeling and EEG analysis interests.
ai.summary: Introduces a biologically informed multi-parametric spectral analysis of electrophysiological recordings that disentangles neural excitability from synaptic kinetics, and demonstrates in a proof-of-concept that it captures hyperexcitability and glutamate reuptake dysfunction signatures characteristic of Alzheimer's disease.

papers.title: Sleep Stage Classification Across Heterogeneous EEG/EOG Channels with Multi-channel Differential Transformer.
papers.abstract: Classification of sleep stages is essential for assessing sleep quality and diagnosing sleep disorders. However, manual inspection of EEG characteristics for each stage is time-consuming and prone to human error. Although machine learning and deep learning methods have been actively developed, they continue to face challenges arising from the non-stationarity and variability of electroencephalography (EEG) and electrooculography (EOG) signals across diverse clinical configurations, often resulting in poor generalization. In this work, we propose SleepDIFFormer, a multi-channel differential transformer framework for heterogeneous EEG-EOG representation learning. SleepDIFFormer is trained across multiple sleep staging datasets, each treated as a source domain, with the goal of generalizing to unseen target domains. Specifically, it employs a Multi-channel Differential Transformer Architecture (MDTA) designed to process raw EEG and EOG signals while incorporating cross-domain alignment. Our approach mitigates spatial and temporal attention noise and learns a domain-invariant EEG-EOG representation through feature distribution alignment across datasets, thereby enhancing generalization to new domains. Empirically, we evaluated SleepDIFFormer on five diverse sleep staging datasets under domain generalization settings and benchmarked it against existing approaches, achieving superior performance. Furthermore, comprehensive ablation analyses and interpretation of the differential attention weights demonstrated their relevance to learning discriminative sleep EEG representations. These findings support the development of more generalizable approaches to automated sleep-stage classification. Our source code and checkpoint are made publicly available at https://github.com/Ben1001409/SleepDIFFormer.

ai.reason: Directly targets generalizable sleep staging across heterogeneous EEG/EOG channels with domain alignment; core relevance, though transformer training may be more GPU-dependent than desired.
ai.summary: Proposed SleepDIFFormer, a multi-channel differential transformer framework using cross-domain alignment for domain-generalizable sleep stage classification from raw heterogeneous EEG/EOG, and reported superior performance versus existing approaches across five sleep staging datasets under domain generalization settings.

papers.title: The ovarian cycle and estradiol modulate cortical network state and auditory entrainment in mice and women
papers.abstract: The human brain is remarkably dynamic, continuously adapting to internal and external signals across rapid and protracted timescales. While both male and female brains are influenced by sex hormones to drive adaptive behavioural and physiological changes, the ovarian cycle in female mammals represents a conserved naturalistic model to understand how hormones such as estradiol (E2) alter cellular and network states to shape brain function. To understand whether and how the ovarian cycle influences sensory cortical processing, we investigated cortical network activity at rest and upon auditory stimulation across the ovarian cycle in mice and human subjects. We recorded EEG activity in men and women and intracortical local field potentials in male and female mice. Female participants were tested during two phases of their ovarian cycle characterized by low E2 levels (early follicular phase in women; late estrus in mice) and high E2 levels (late follicular phase in women; proestrus in mice). Across species, high endogenous or exogenous estradiol was associated with a steeper aperiodic power spectral slope, indicating decreased excitatory/inhibitory drive and attenuated auditory entrainment following a 40Hz stimulation. At the single-cell level, high E2 selectively increased the baseline and sustained 40-Hz firing of putative fast-spiking interneurons while reducing their temporal coherence during both spontaneous and stimulus-evoked activity, suggesting that E2 enhances inhibitory tone, while disrupting the temporal coordination of inhibitory networks. Altogether, these findings demonstrate that estradiol dynamically modulates cortical network states and auditory responsiveness. This underscores the necessity of investigating hormone-brain coupling as an evolutionarily conserved model essential for yielding translational insights into sex-specific neurobiology.

ai.topic: Aperiodic spectral slope across hormone states
ai.reason: Cross-species EEG/LFP with aperiodic spectral slope and network-state analysis aligns with spectral and state modeling interests and spans animal-to-human translation.
ai.summary: Compared cortical network activity at rest and during 40 Hz auditory stimulation across low- and high-estradiol ovarian cycle phases in mice and women (with EEG and intracortical LFP), finding that high endogenous or exogenous estradiol steepened the aperiodic spectral slope and attenuated auditory entrainment, while increasing fast-spiking interneuron 40-Hz firing but reducing its temporal coherence.

papers.title: EEG Pathology Detection via Clinical Concept Bottleneck Models
papers.abstract: Deep learning models for electroencephalography (EEG) pathology detection achieve competitive accuracy but offer limited interpretability. In this paper, we introduce concept bottleneck models (CBMs) for EEG pathology detection which use clinical EEG biomarkers computed analytically from the signal as a bottleneck to be used for prediction. Those concepts include band power, spectral ratios, alpha peak frequency and amplitude, hemispheric asymmetry and phase locking values. With the backbone based on shallow convolutional neural network (CNN), we compare a black box baseline with two variants of CBMs. The hybrid variant is a classifier receives a residual projection of the backbone features. The pure variant is a CBM where the classifier receives only the predicted concepts. Models are evaluated on abnormality detection and dementia classification followed by concept prediction quality and leakage analysis. Both CBMs approach the baseline on TUAB (82.7-82.9% vs 83.6%) and are 2-5 percentage points lower on CAUEEG (57.9-60.5% vs 62.7%). The pure CBM exhibits concept fidelity concern where the predicted concepts deviate from their ground truth values. Replacing them with their true values causes severe cost on accuracy by 26 and 22 points on TUAB and CAUEEG. The concept fidelity concern is mitigated by increasing the weight of the concept loss to match the ground truth concepts. the mitigation comes with small accuracy cost on TUAB but a relatively larger cost on CAUEEG. The code of the experiments and full logs are available at https://www.github.com/mhmdrdwn/cbm.

ai.topic: Interpretable EEG pathology detection via concept bottlenecks
ai.reason: Uses clinically interpretable spectral concepts and shallow CNNs for EEG classification, aligning with interpretable feature extraction and lightweight model priorities.
ai.summary: This study introduces concept bottleneck models for EEG pathology detection that use analytically computed clinical EEG biomarkers (e.g., band power, spectral ratios, phase locking values) as an interpretable bottleneck. The models approach black-box baseline accuracy on TUAB (82.7-82.9% vs 83.6%) but show lower performance on CAUEEG (57.9-60.5% vs 62.7%), with a pure CBM variant exhibiting concept fidelity concerns mitigated by increasing concept loss weight.

papers.title: A Humanized Mouse Model of DRPLA Recapitulates Epilepsy and Demonstrates Antisense Oligonucleotide-Mediated Disease Modification
papers.abstract: Dentatorubral-pallidoluysian atrophy (DRPLA) is an ultra-rare progressive myoclonus epilepsy caused by a glutamine-coding CAG repeat expansion in atrophin-1 (ATN1). Mutant ATN1 (mATN1) expression results in symptoms that inversely correlate to CAG-expansion size: young-onset cases have the most CAG repeats and developmental delay, high-frequency treatment-resistant seizures, and early mortality. We sought to characterize the seizure susceptibility of a fully humanized ATN1 mouse expressing human mATN1 with 112 CAG repeats to then assess therapeutic antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) intervention on seizure-related outcomes. Atn1Q112/+ or wild-type (WT) mice were treated with investigational ASO targeting human, CAG-expanded, ATN1 or saline (P2 and then again at 4 weeks-old) before acute seizure testing, ataxia profiling, and chronic in vivo video-EEG recording for spontaneous seizures up to 8 weeks-old. Saline-treated Atn1Q112/+ mice were more seizure prone with early death. However, ASO administration to Atn1Q112/+ mice normalized seizure threshold, decreased ataxia, and protected against early death. Atn1Q112/+ mice exhibited spontaneous behavioral seizures recorded over 2 weeks, which were absent in ASO-treated Atn1Q112/+ and WT mice, with a specific mATN1 expression-driven decrease in delta and theta EEG frequencies. Atn1Q112/+ mice are highly seizure prone, validating this model for DRPLA epilepsy. ATN1 represents a novel epilepsy-related risk factor for therapeutic investigation.

ai.reason: Chronic in vivo video-EEG in mice with seizure quantification is directly relevant to animal EEG recording and analysis pipelines, though the primary contribution is therapeutic.
ai.summary: Characterized seizure susceptibility in a fully humanized Atn1Q112/+ DRPLA mouse model and tested an antisense oligonucleotide targeting CAG-expanded ATN1. Saline-treated mutants showed increased seizure propensity and early death, while ASO treatment normalized seizure threshold, reduced ataxia, prevented spontaneous behavioral seizures, and protected against early death.

papers.title: Sleep underestimation and subjective sleep appraisal: Limited value of routine polysomnographic and electroencephalographic features.
papers.abstract: Whether routine polysomnographic (PSG) and electroencephalographic (EEG) features distinguish patients who underestimate sleep remains unclear. We examined associations of clinical, subjective, PSG, and EEG features with sleep underestimation and tested whether EEG features added discrimination beyond a parsimonious three-predictor baseline model. We analysed 225 adults undergoing clinically indicated in-laboratory PSG in this single-centre retrospective cross-sectional study. The misperception index ([objective - subjective total sleep time]/objective total sleep time) was dichotomised at the cohort median (0.148) and analysed continuously. Group differences across 717 variables underwent Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction. Out-of-fold (OOF) discrimination was compared between a three-predictor baseline model (sleep quality, Epworth Sleepiness Scale score, and age) and an EEG-enhanced model; continuous-index analyses were exploratory. Fifty-six participants (24.9%) overestimated sleep. Objective total sleep time did not differ between groups, whereas self-rated sleep quality did (q = 0.002). None of 600 EEG features survived FDR correction (smallest q = 0.064). At the median threshold, OOF areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) were 0.6786 (baseline) and 0.6564 (EEG-enhanced; ΔAUC = -0.0221; paired DeLong P = 0.4483). Across 50 repeated partitions, median ΔAUC was -0.0261 for EEG features and +0.0096 for four macrostructural PSG variables. Obstructive sleep apnoea prevalence did not differ significantly between groups. Self-rated sleep quality was more consistently associated with sleep underestimation than routine PSG and EEG features. EEG features did not demonstrate incremental OOF discrimination beyond the baseline model. Subjective sleep appraisal should be assessed alongside PSG; underlying mechanisms require prospective investigation.

ai.reason: Large PSG/EEG feature analysis with out-of-fold model comparison; relevant sleep context but negative findings limit methodological usefulness.
ai.summary: In a single-centre retrospective cross-sectional study of 225 adults undergoing clinical polysomnography, self-rated sleep quality was more consistently associated with sleep underestimation than routine PSG/EEG features, and none of 600 EEG features survived FDR correction; an EEG-enhanced model added no out-of-fold discrimination beyond a three-predictor baseline (AUC 0.6564 vs. 0.6786).

papers.title: A self-organized QTPat-based feature-engineering framework for subject-independent classification of English- and Turkish-associated EEG signals.
papers.abstract: Our primary aim is to develop an automated feature-engineering framework for subject-independent classification of EEG recordings acquired from English-speaking and Turkish-speaking participant cohorts. Drawing inspiration from a quantum tunnel pattern called QTPat, we introduced a novel approach of dynamically generating directed graphs to extract textural features. For our experiments, we utilized an EEG dataset containing 1652 English sentence-EEG pairs and 1600 Turkish sentence-EEG pairs. These signals were recorded from 20 English-speaking and 20 Turkish subjects who were presented with standardized sentences in their respective native languages. During the experiments, the participants were instructed to carefully contemplate each sentence while wearing a mobile brain cap system that acquired 14-channel EEG signals. Our preprocessing pipeline involved subjecting the EEG signals to multiple filtered wavelet packet decompositions, using both 6 Daubechies and 6 symlet wavelet filters. Subsequently, we extracted textural and statistical features employing the QTPat model, along with 20 statistical moments. To enhance discriminative power, we applied neighborhood component analysis and the Chi2-function to select the most relevant features. The k-nearest neighbor classifier was then employed to calculate predictive vectors. To further refine the results, we introduced an iterative hard majority voting scheme, generating additional voted vectors. Finally, we utilized a greedy algorithm to select the best-channel-wise and overall model results. Using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation (LOSO CV), the proposed framework achieved 96.37% classification accuracy using four selected EEG channels. These findings demonstrate that the QTPat-based architecture can discriminate the two language-associated EEG cohorts under subject-independent evaluation. However, because language and participant population are coupled in the available dataset, the present results should not be interpreted as definitive evidence of language-specific neural decoding. Further studies using within-subject bilingual experimental designs are required to determine whether the identified EEG patterns specifically reflect language-related neural processing.

ai.reason: Feature-engineering pipeline with wavelet-packet decomposition and subject-independent classification is relevant to interpretable feature extraction, but the quantum-pattern novelty is idiosyncratic.
ai.summary: Introduced a QTPat-based feature-engineering framework for subject-independent EEG classification of English- and Turkish-associated signals, achieving 96.37% accuracy with four channels using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation. The authors note that the results are not definitive evidence of language-specific neural decoding due to confounding between language and participant population.

papers.title: Neural mechanisms of training in Brain-Computer Interface: A Biophysical modeling approach
papers.abstract: Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) is a system that translates neural activity into commands, allowing direct communication between brain and external devices. Despite its clinical application, BCIs are unable to robustly capture the intent of the subjects due to limited understanding of the neural mechanisms underlying BCI control. To address this, we introduce a biophysical linear neural mass model to investigate the associated neural mechanisms of motor imagery BCI (MI-BCI) by modulating the scale-free spectral characteristics of afferent inputs. We tailor this motor imagery neural mass model (mi-NMM) to simulate both MI and resting-state activity and apply it to a cohort of 19 healthy subjects trained over four sessions, during which magnetoencephalography and electroencephalography signals were simultaneously recorded. Task-dependent significant modulation of scale-free cortical dynamics reveals training-induced excitatory-inhibitory (E/I) reconfiguration during BCI training, shifting from widespread cortical to targeted sensorimotor recruitment. The modeled intra-regional E/I interaction strengths and excitatory population time constants capture condition and session-related changes in neural activation in the relevant areas of the sensorimotor cortex, where MI-related desynchronization and synchronization are associated with excitatory population time constants. Thus, these mechanistic findings provide new insights into the underlying neural mechanisms of MI-BCI, paving the way for tailored BCI training protocols.

ai.topic: Biophysical neural mass model of BCI training
ai.reason: Dynamical/biophysical modeling of scale-free spectral dynamics, which aligns with state-space/dynamical-system interests, but BCI-training focus is peripheral.
ai.summary: Introduced a biophysical linear neural mass model (mi-NMM) of motor imagery BCI fitted to simultaneous MEG/EEG from 19 healthy subjects across four training sessions; task-dependent modulation of scale-free dynamics revealed training-induced excitatory-inhibitory reconfiguration shifting from widespread cortical to targeted sensorimotor recruitment, with excitatory population time constants linked to MI-related desynchronization and synchronization.

papers.title: Aperiodic neural activity predicts cortical excitability in TMS-EEG
papers.abstract: Background: Fluctuating cortical excitability states are inherent to and critical for brain function. They can be probed non-invasively using transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) combined with electroencephalography (EEG) by measuring early local TMS-evoked potentials (EL-TEPs). Pre-stimulus periodic neural activity can predict fluctuating excitability states. To what extent aperiodic neural activity represents a marker of cortical excitability has not been explored. Objectives: We investigated the relationship between pre-stimulus aperiodic and periodic neural activity and EL-TEP amplitude in both the primary motor cortex (M1) and dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC). Methods: Single-pulse TMS was delivered to the left M1 or left DLPFC in 29 and 11 healthy adults, respectively, while EEG was recorded simultaneously. Pre-stimulus EEG was parameterized into aperiodic and periodic components to extract the aperiodic exponent (slope of 1/f-like activity), alpha power (8-13 Hz), and beta power (13-30 Hz). EL-TEP peak-to-peak amplitudes were extracted from approximately 20-65 ms after the TMS pulse. Results: Aperiodic exponent showed a strong negative relationship with EL-TEP amplitude in both M1 and DLPFC, with steeper 1/f-like slopes associated with smaller EL-TEP amplitudes. Inconsistent relationships were found between alpha and beta power with EL-TEP amplitude across the two regions. Conclusions: These findings indicate that pre-stimulus aperiodic neural activity influences cortical excitability in both motor and prefrontal areas. Notably, the aperiodic exponent exhibited stronger associations with cortical excitability compared to periodic alpha or beta power. Brain-state-dependent protocols may benefit from real-time extraction of aperiodic exponent as a target feature to improve the precision and efficacy of TMS.

ai.reason: Uses aperiodic/periodic spectral parameterization, which is transferable to neural time-series analysis, but the TMS-EEG excitability context is adjacent to core interests.
ai.summary: Single-pulse TMS-EEG in healthy adults (n=29 M1, n=11 DLPFC) showed a strong negative relationship between the pre-stimulus aperiodic exponent and early local TMS-evoked potential amplitude in both regions, with steeper 1/f-like slopes associated with smaller EL-TEPs and inconsistent alpha/beta power relationships.

papers.title: Should I "stay" or should I "go"? Influence of an anticipated stop on cortical correlates of overground walking.
papers.abstract: Real-world walking frequently requires pedestrians to maintain proactive inhibition to safely navigate unpredictable environments. While cortical modulations occurring during locomotion under environmental uncertainty are well-established, the specific proactive mechanisms underlying this state of inhibitory anticipation remain unexplored. This study aimed to investigate the behavioral and cortical shifts associated with anticipating a stop during overground walking. Fourteen healthy young adults performed fluent and cautious walking tasks with an expected stop. Cortical activity and trunk acceleration were recorded using a 32-channel mobile electroencephalography and an integrated accelerometer. Step-1 latency and step-interval variability were calculated via heel strike detection. Gait-phase-related power modulations were computed, and spectral principal component analysis was applied to attenuate artifacts. The results revealed that cautious walking significantly increased step-interval variability, whereas step-1 latency remained unaffected. At the cortical level, left frontotemporal areas exhibited an attenuated and delayed theta desynchronization during the swing phase. Furthermore, centroparietal regions demonstrated an altered temporal profile of alpha and beta synchronization, characterized by enhanced late-stance synchronization and reduced swing-phase synchronization. The present findings suggest that anticipating a potential stop may alter the rhythmic consistency of gait and reorganize phase-specific cortical dynamics. Being prepared to stop may shift the neural control of automated locomotion toward active monitoring, highlighting the relevance of proactive inhibition during everyday mobility.

ai.reason: Mobile EEG with artifact attenuation and spectral PCA; some signal-processing relevance but locomotion context is adjacent.
ai.summary: Mobile EEG and accelerometry in 14 healthy adults showed that anticipating a stop during overground walking increased step-interval variability and reorganized gait-phase cortical dynamics, with attenuated/delayed left frontotemporal theta desynchronization during swing and altered centroparietal alpha/beta synchronization. The authors interpret this as a shift from automated locomotion toward active monitoring via proactive inhibition.

papers.title: Dorsolateral prefrontal TMS-evoked N100 as a neurophysiological correlate of symptom change in adolescent depression.
papers.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is highly prevalent in adolescence. Up to 30% of patients insufficiently benefit from first-line treatments, underscoring the need for improved treatment strategies and better understanding of pathophysiology. In depression, an imbalance between cortical excitation and inhibition in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), assessed by the TMS-evoked N100 potential, is suggested as one of several contributing neurobiological mechanisms. While elevated N100 amplitudes have been observed in depressed adults and adolescents, its association with symptom change remains insufficiently investigated. In a randomized controlled trial, N = 54 adolescents (38 girls, 16 boys) with MDD received six weeks of whole body vibration training (exercising on a vibrating plate that triggers involuntary muscle contractions through a neurological reflex) or light stretching as add-on treatments to treatment as usual. TMS-EEG was applied before and after the intervention to assess N100 amplitudes over the left and right DLPFC. Depressive symptoms were measured using the Children's Depression Rating Scale-Revised. Changes in N100 amplitudes were analyzed using repeated measures ANOVA. Multiple regression analyses with intervention group as predictor examined associations between changes in N100 amplitudes and depressive symptoms, including sex as moderator and a subsequent girls-only analysis. Across both groups, N100 amplitudes significantly decreased from pre-to post-intervention. No differential effects between interventions were observed. Reductions in right-hemispheric N100 amplitudes were significantly associated with improvements in depressive symptoms. This association reached statistical significance in girls. Our findings support the N100 as a candidate neurophysiological correlate of depressive symptom improvement.

ai.reason: TMS-EEG evoked potential analysis with repeated measures; adjacent to EEG methods but focused on clinical depression and not on sleep or lightweight algorithms.
ai.summary: In a randomized controlled trial of 54 adolescents with major depressive disorder, TMS-EEG showed that TMS-evoked dorsolateral prefrontal N100 amplitudes decreased from pre- to post-intervention; reductions in right-hemispheric N100 were significantly associated with improved depressive symptoms, particularly in girls. The authors propose the N100 as a candidate neurophysiological correlate of symptom change.

papers.title: Coupled cardio-pulmonary-cerebral functional dynamics for high-quality cardiopulmonary resuscitation.
papers.abstract: Cardiac arrest (CA) is one of the leading causes of death worldwide. High-quality cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) can effectively improve the survival rate of CA patients. To find physiological indicators particularly those reflecting the cerebral function to assess the quality of CPR is a challenging issue. This study aimed to investigate the cardio-pulmonary-cerebral coupling to assess the physiological status of CA patients during CPR. Arterial blood pressure (ABP), electroencephalography (EEG), and end-tidal carbon dioxide partial pressure (PETCO2) signals collected in porcine experiments were divided into four periods: Baseline, CA, CPR, and recovery of spontaneous circulation (ROSC). Cross recurrence quantification analysis (CRQA) was applied to examine the dynamical couplings of ABP-EEG, ABP-PETCO2, and EEG-PETCO2 during the four periods. In addition, a joint recurrence quantification analysis (JRQA) was applied to examine the cardio-pulmonary-cerebral dynamical coupling across the ABP, EEG, and PETCO2 during the four periods. The RR, DET, ENTR, and Lmax of ABP-PETCO2 coupling using CRQA were significantly lower during CA than during Baseline, and these parameters were significantly higher during CPR and ROSC than during CA. The RR and DET of ABP-EEG and PETCO2-EEG coupling were highest during CPR and lowest during CA (p < 0.05), and they were higher in the T7 cortical region during Baseline than other regions (p < 0.05). The RR, DET, and ENTR of ABP-PETCO2-EEG coupling using JRQA showed significantly higher values during CA than during the other periods, and the Lmax of ABP-PETCO2-EEG coupling exhibited significantly lower values during CA than during the other periods. Dynamical coupling of ABP-PETCO2-EEG could reflect the physiological states of CA patients. The T7 cortical region was identified as the most sensitive to the CPR process. This study sheds light on the value of cardio-pulmonary-cerebral dynamical coupling in indication of the effects of CPR and may play a role in screening the function of vital organs during emergency treatment.
papers.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine

ai.reason: Applies recurrence quantification to multi-signal coupling in porcine data; dynamical-system angle is mildly transferable but domain is far from EEG sleep analysis.
ai.summary: Using porcine cardiac arrest experiments, this study applied cross- and joint recurrence quantification analysis to arterial blood pressure, EEG, and end-tidal CO2 to quantify cardio-pulmonary-cerebral coupling across baseline, cardiac arrest, CPR, and ROSC. Coupling measures distinguished physiological states, and the T7 cortical region was identified as most sensitive to the CPR process.

papers.title: Altered resting-state EEG microstate dynamics are associated with auditory hallucinations in patients with major depressive disorder.
papers.abstract: Auditory hallucination experiences are an understudied but clinically significant feature of major depressive disorder (MDD). Although EEG microstate abnormalities have been reported in MDD, their relationship with auditory hallucination experiences remains unclear. This study investigated resting-state EEG microstate dynamics associated with auditory hallucination experiences in first-episode MDD. A total of 182 first-episode patients with MDD and 95 healthy controls underwent resting-state EEG recordings. Patients were classified according to lifetime history of auditory hallucination experiences into those with (AH+, n = 42) and without (AH-, n = 140) such experiences. Patients were either psychotropic medication-naïve or minimally medicated (<2 weeks of cumulative exposure). Microstate parameters were compared among groups. ANCOVA and hierarchical binary logistic regression were performed to examine associations with auditory hallucination experiences. Only microstate C occurrence was significantly higher in the AH+ group than in both the AH- and healthy control groups after multiple-comparison correction. This difference remained significant after adjustment for age, sex, education, and depression severity. Hierarchical logistic regression showed that higher microstate C occurrence was independently associated with auditory hallucination experiences (OR = 1.773, 95% CI: 1.211-2.595, p = 0.003), but not with hallucination severity. Its discriminatory ability was modest (AUC = 0.614, 95% CI: 0.516-0.711). In first-episode MDD, a lifetime history of auditory hallucination experiences was associated with increased microstate C occurrence. This finding suggests that altered microstate C dynamics may represent an electrophysiological correlate of auditory hallucination experiences, warranting further investigation.

ai.reason: Microstate dynamics are a transferable state-space-like EEG measure, but the clinical auditory-hallucination application is adjacent to the researcher's interests.
ai.summary: In 182 first-episode major depressive disorder patients and 95 healthy controls, resting-state EEG microstate C occurrence was significantly higher in patients with lifetime auditory hallucination experiences than in those without and in controls, and remained independently associated with such experiences (OR = 1.773) after covariate adjustment, though discrimination was modest (AUC = 0.614).

papers.title: Supramodal Coding of Detection and Confidence in the Human Cortex
papers.abstract: Perception is inherently multisensory, yet it remains unclear whether the brain detects stimuli and evaluates confidence in these detections using circuits shared across senses or circuits specific to each modality. Prior evidence is limited: scalp electrophysiology cannot localize where a shared code operates, whereas functional imaging cannot resolve its timing. We recorded intracranial activity (stereoelectroencephalography) in eight patients with epilepsy who performed a near-threshold audiovisual detection task in which they reported, on each trial, whether a visual, auditory, or audiovisual stimulus was present and rated their confidence, both overall and separately for each modality. Analyzing high-gamma activity at the single-channel and region-of-interest levels, we found that stimulus detection involved a broadly distributed, largely supramodal set of cortical regions responding regardless of modality, including the insula, dorsomedial prefrontal cortex, and superior temporal gyrus. Multivariate decoders trained to distinguish detected from undetected stimuli in one modality generalized to the other modality, indicating a shared detection code within these regions. Confidence relied on a more mixed architecture but was also substantially supramodal. Finally, the auditory cortex encoded confidence information about its non-preferred (visual) modality, with a similar effect in the visual cortex for auditory confidence, suggesting that the involvement of sensory cortices in confidence is not confined to its preferred input.

ai.reason: Intracranial decoding and multivariate methods transferable in principle, but invasive human cognitive task far from sleep/animal EEG tooling.
ai.summary: Intracranial stereoelectroencephalography in eight epilepsy patients performing a near-threshold audiovisual detection task revealed a largely supramodal cortical detection code (including insula, dorsomedial prefrontal cortex, superior temporal gyrus) whose multivariate decoders generalized across modalities, and a substantially supramodal confidence architecture including cross-modal confidence coding in sensory cortices.

papers.title: Corollary discharge dysfunction in auditory verbal hallucinations: N100 suppression measured with semi-dry electrodes.
papers.abstract: Corollary discharge dysfunction in patients with auditory verbal hallucinations (AVH) is reflected in failure to attenuate the N100 event-related potential. Previous research has shown mixed findings regarding N100 suppression and hallucination severity, generally using broad symptom scales rather than AVH-specific measures. This study investigated corollary discharge and its relationship with comprehensively characterized auditory hallucinations. Corollary discharge was investigated in 14 patients with persistent auditory hallucinations and 15 healthy controls using an EEG paradigm using semi-dry electrodes where participants self-generated sounds in a "talk" condition and listened to playback in a "listen" condition. N100 suppression was calculated as the peak-amplitude difference (μV) between talk and listen in the 60-150 ms window. Auditory hallucinations were assessed with the Psychotic Symptom Rating Scales Auditory Hallucination Subscale (PSYRATS-AHS). Between-group analysis of the fronto-central ROI (Fz-Cz) showed a statistically non-significant trend toward greater N100 suppression in healthy controls compared to AVH patients (p = 0.095, Cohen's d = 0.64). N100 suppression showed significant negative correlation with hallucination severity in the AVH group (r = -0.54, p = 0.047). Hallucination severity is related to impaired corollary discharge mechanisms, supporting its role as a mechanistic basis for auditory hallucinations. The preliminary correlation with PSYRATS-AHS suggests potential value in using symptom-specific assessment tools in research on auditory hallucinations, warranting replication in larger samples.

ai.reason: Event-related potential and electrode technology relevant to practical EEG, but clinical psychiatry focus and small sample limit transferability.
ai.summary: In 14 patients with persistent auditory verbal hallucinations and 15 healthy controls, N100 suppression during self-generated versus played-back sounds was measured with semi-dry EEG electrodes; healthy controls showed a non-significant trend toward greater suppression, and suppression correlated negatively with hallucination severity (r = -0.54, p = 0.047). The authors interpret this as support for impaired corollary discharge as a mechanistic basis for auditory hallucinations, pending larger-sample replication.

papers.title: Retrospective attention strengthens a report-independent neural signature of visual perception
papers.abstract: Visual perception can remain modifiable after a stimulus has disappeared, but it is unknown at which processing stage a post-stimulus cue operates: on the lingering sensory trace, on the perceptual representation, or on later decision and report processes. We used masked retrospective cues to establish the behavioral effect and a Report/No-report EEG design to locate its processing stage. In Experiments 1 and 2, retrospective cues improved orientation discrimination even when masking reduced cue-location accuracy to near chance. In Experiment 3, valid cues increased EEG evidence for the target in a late interval, without the early enhancement expected from an early, additive sensory interaction. Without explicit target report, valid cues still strengthened the neural representation of the target, and a decoder trained only on no-report trials predicted trial-by-trial visibility and orientation discrimination in separate report trials, arguing against a purely report-contingent decisional account. When report was required, the cueing benefit appeared mainly in additional report-specific signals, which also predicted visibility most strongly. Retrospective attention thus strengthens a report-independent visual target representation, and explicit report can amplify this effect.

papers.title: Responses to unannounced rule changes in adults with developmental disabilities: A community-based pilot study with consumer-grade EEG
papers.abstract: Unannounced changes in rules or environments often precede challenging behavior and limit community participation for adults with developmental disabilities, yet their responses to change have rarely been quantified directly. We recruited adults with developmental disabilities, including those with intellectual disability, at a community day-service center. We administered a probabilistic reversal learning task and recorded resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) via a 14-channel wireless EEG system. Among the 12 adults who performed the task, total errors were comparable across participants (range 31-57), whereas a switch bias index, contrasting perseverative errors (persisting with the previously correct option) with regressive errors (failing to maintain the newly correct option), ranged from -0.96 to +0.91. In the 9 participants included in resting-state EEG analyses, a flatter aperiodic spectrum over the frontal cluster (preregistered, but selected as the focus post hoc) was associated with fewer switches after negative feedback ({rho} = .80) and more perseverative errors ({rho} = -.72). The preregistered parieto-occipital cluster showed the same direction ({rho} = .69, 95% confidence interval [-.11, .97], n = 8), which was opposite to the preregistered prediction. Frontal alpha peak amplitude was associated with accuracy ({rho} = .77), and the between-run reliability of resting-state measures was .82-.99. These findings provide preliminary evidence that EEG recorded in community settings can capture individual differences in how people respond to change. Field measurement that includes people with intellectual disability may help extend the evidence base for the Sustainable Development Goals of good health and well-being (SDG 3) and reduced inequalities (SDG 10).

papers.title: Normative data of laser evoked potentials using Nd:YAP laser.
papers.abstract: To establish a robust multi-centre normative database for Nd:YAP laser-evoked potentials (LEPs) across distal and proximal stimulation sites, and to quantify the impact of laser spot size (energy density) and demographic factors on LEP parameters. One hundred nine healthy adults (57 females) were recruited from three centres (Geneva, Lyon, Saint-Etienne). Nd:YAP laser pulses were delivered with a 3-mm beam (Centre 1) or 4-mm beam (Centres 2-3). LEPs were recorded from standard EEG sites (including Fz/Cz/Pz and contralateral temporal leads). Stimulation sites included hand dorsum (n = 109), foot dorsum (n = 80), thigh and upper neck (both n = 43). N1, N2, and P2 latencies and amplitudes were measured and normal limits estimated as mean ± 99.9% confidence interval. ANCOVA (age-corrected) tested spot-size effects; repeated-measures ANOVA tested site effects; correlations assessed age/height associations. The vertex N2-P2 complex was consistently recorded across centres and sites (100% for hand, thigh, neck; ∼97% for foot). N1 detection was less consistent, particularly with larger spot size and at the foot. Smaller spot size (higher energy density) yielded shorter N2/P2 latencies and larger N2-P2 amplitudes for hand stimulation, and shorter P2 latency for foot stimulation. Sex and height showed no significant effects. Increasing age was associated with longer N2/P2 latencies and reduced N2-P2 amplitudes for distal sites, with minimal age effects at proximal sites. This study provides the most comprehensive Nd:YAP LEP normative dataset to date, including distal and proximal sites and spot-size-specific reference limits. These data support standardized, high-specificity clinical interpretation of LEPs for assessing small-fibre and spinothalamic pathway dysfunction.

papers.title: Spectral power and functional connectivity of resting EEG in people exposed to armed conflict and controls
papers.abstract: Exposure to armed conflict can leave persistent effects on mental health, yet its neurophysiological correlates remain poorly characterized, particularly in populations exposed to prolonged violence outside narrowly defined post traumatic stress disorder samples. Here we examined resting state electroencephalographic activity in 122 Colombian adults, including 74 participants exposed to armed conflict and 48 controls. Eyes closed EEG was analysed for 240 seconds per participant. We quantified absolute and relative spectral power across delta, theta, alpha and beta bands and regional functional connectivity using weighted phase lag index in theta, alpha and beta. Group comparisons were adjusted for age, education, sex and assessment year, with correction across 78 EEG contrasts. Median occipital and global alpha power was lower in exposed participants, although adjusted estimates were close to the null and confidence intervals were broad. Temporal theta relative power was lower in exposed participants at nominal significance, but this association did not survive Holm correction. No spectral power or regional connectivity contrast remained significant after multiple testing correction. Exploratory associations between EEG measures and MoCA performance were modest in participants with confirmed scores. These findings provide a systematic characterization of resting EEG after exposure to armed conflict in a population shaped by prolonged violence and displacement. They also indicate that large or widespread alterations in resting spectral power and connectivity were not detectable with the current sample and analytical framework, while defining candidate signals and methodological priorities for larger studies of conflict related brain health.

papers.title: Differing subjective and psychophysiological response patterns to a music-based auditory intervention for anxiety.
papers.abstract: Anxiety comprises partially dissociable cognitive and somatic components, yet it remains unclear whether brief interventions modulate these systems in parallel. This randomized controlled trial examined subjective and psychophysiological responses to a brief music-based auditory intervention relative to an active auditory control (pink noise) in undergraduate students reporting recent generalized anxiety symptoms. Participants (N = 83) were randomized to the auditory intervention or pink noise. Cognitive and somatic anxiety were assessed before and after the intervention, while salivary cortisol, heart rate variability (HRV), and electroencephalography (EEG) indexed endocrine, autonomic, and neural processes. Cortisol showed a significant Condition × Time interaction, with larger reductions following the auditory intervention. Midline theta power also exhibited a significant Condition × Time interaction, reflecting opposing patterns of change across conditions, although within-condition changes were only significant in the pink noise condition. Cognitive anxiety, somatic anxiety, affective arousal, frontal alpha lateralization, and HRV did not show significant differential baseline-to-post change. During listening, HRV increased across conditions, but the Condition × Epoch interaction observed in the primary growth model was not retained when participant-specific slopes were included. Together, these findings indicate differing patterns of response across levels of analysis, with broad reductions in self-reported anxiety and arousal across both auditory conditions and greater condition sensitivity in the primary cortisol and midline-theta analyses. Because the cortisol and theta interactions were not retained in models including all physiologically valid observations, these condition-dependent findings should be interpreted cautiously.

papers.title: Selection vs. integration task demands shape the similarity of information neural coding
papers.abstract: Attention is a function that enables selection and integration of multiple sources of information. However, how these demands influence neural coding of information is not well understood. In this study we used EEG to examine how the selection vs. integration of stimuli shapes the content and geometry reflected on neural patterns, during both preparation and target processing. Participants performed a size judgement task in a cue-target paradigm that, depending on the block, required judging either the size of a selected item and ignoring the additional stimulus or integrating both to respond. Decoding analyses showed that under selection demands, categorical templates of the cued stimulus were active during preparation and target coding, contrasting with integration, where patterns linked to the cued category could be observed only during preparation. Notably, RSA suggested specific exemplar encoding during its processing, which was sustained also across the post-stimulus window during selection, yet was not observable under integration contexts. Our results also suggest that attentional demands shape the similarity between stimulus categories by increasing the distance between selected stimuli and distractors or by reducing it between to-be-integrated information. Overall, this study uncovers the dynamics of stimulus encoding under selection and integration demands, offering crucial advances to understand how top-down processes shape information representation in the human brain.

papers.title: Cooperative processing of visual threat across collicular pathways
papers.abstract: Rapid defensive actions require the transformation of sensory cues into appropriate motor responses. The superior colliculus is central to this transformation, containing defined cell-types that form parallel output pathways linking visual inputs to distinct behaviors. However, whether these pathways act independently or cooperate remains unclear. Here we combine cell-type-specific inhibition, large-scale electrophysiology, and functional ultrasound imaging to determine how these pathways contribute to visually evoked defensive behaviors. Inhibiting either narrow-field or wide-field neurons impaired escape to overhead visual threats, demonstrating that both pathways contribute to escape. Recordings from downstream targets revealed a compact representation in the deeper layers of the superior colliculus that selectively distinguished visual stimuli associated with escape, whereas the lateral posterior thalamus contained a broader representation of visual stimuli. The representation of visual threat in the deeper layers of the superior colliculus predicted escape initiation and vigor in freely moving animals. Across the brain, functional ultrasound imaging showed that visual stimuli recruited distinct patterns of activity that could not be explained by response magnitude alone or by the contribution of single cell-types. Together, these results reveal a cooperative circuit architecture in which parallel pathways carry distinct but complementary signals that jointly support visually evoked escape.

papers.title: Phasic and tonic pain serve distinct functions during adaptive behaviour
papers.abstract: Pain drives self-protective behaviour, and evolutionary theories suggest it acts over different timescales to serve distinct functions. Whilst phasic pain provides a teaching signal to drive avoidance of new injury, tonic pain is argued to support recuperative behaviour, for instance by reducing motivational vigour. We test this hypothesis in an immersive virtual reality EEG foraging task where subjects harvested fruit in a forest: some fruit elicited brief phasic pain to the grasping hand, and this reduced choice probability. Simultaneously, tonic pressure pain to the contralateral upper arm was associated with reduced action velocities. This could be explained by a free-operant computational framework that formalises and quantifies the function of tonic and phasic pain in terms of motivational vigour and decision value. Additional analyses examined the relationship between model parameters, subjective ratings, and physiological and neural responses. Overall, the results show how tonic and phasic pain subserve distinct objective motivational functions that support harm minimisation during ongoing adaptive behaviour.

papers.title: A Reproducible Safety Assessment Model for Concurrent Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation with Implanted Intracranial Electroencephalography Electrodes.
papers.abstract: Concurrent transcranial magnetic stimulation and intracranial EEG (TMS-sEEG) offers a powerful approach for interrogating human brain circuits with high spatiotemporal resolution. However, standardized safety testing procedures for TMS in the presence of implanted electrodes are lacking. To establish and validate a reproducible methodological framework for assessing TMS safety with sEEG hardware, addressing potential risks of electrode displacement, heating, and secondary current induction. A conductive agarose phantom implanted with clinical-grade platinum sEEG electrodes was exposed to single-pulse TMS (0.4 Hz), repetitive TMS (1-50 Hz), and intermittent theta burst stimulation. Electrode displacement was quantified via high-speed video and motion tracking. Temperature changes were measured with fiber-optic thermal probes positioned at stimulated electrode contacts. Induced voltages were recorded using an oscilloscope and intracranial EEG hardware, and secondary current and charge density were calculated from oscilloscope outputs and impedance measurements. sEEG lead displacement remained micrometer-scale across stimulation conditions, with a maximum transient displacement of 10.99 μm and a maximum 1-s mean displacement from the pre-TMS position of 16.27 μm. Temperature changes remained well within the 2°C safety threshold across all tested conditions; in the primary temperature series, the maximum observed increase was 0.073°C. Induced voltages and charge densities remained below established safety limits, exhibiting consistent exponential decay with increasing distance from the coil. All stimulation conditions, including those exceeding typical clinical ranges, remained well within safety margins. Under the tested conditions in a controlled phantom environment, TMS exposure produced micrometer-scale transient and longer-timescale displacement, temperature changes within established safety thresholds, and charge densities within established safety thresholds. This validated methodological pipeline provides a standardized framework for future safety experiments involving TMS and implanted devices and supports continued development of TMS-sEEG as a tool for studying human brain circuitry and neuromodulation.

papers.title: Audience Gaze and Felt Social Connection With Individual Performers During Live Dance.
papers.abstract: In everyday social interactions, our looking behavior reflects our relationships with others, but the role that social perception plays for engagement with the performing arts is understudied. We commissioned the durational, community-focused, 16-h dance performance How Shall We Begin Again?, comprising a continuous relay of individual improvised performances by 50 people over 2 consecutive days. During the performance, we recorded eye movements and mobile EEG from 88 audience members who entered and exited the performance space freely. Audience members reported on their experience of individual performers immediately after leaving the performance space. Gaze toward people in the scene showed a significant indirect association with felt social connection through self-reported focus on individual performers; the overall gaze-connection association, however, was not statistically significant. Individual differences in mind wandering, dance experience, and empathy were associated with gaze and engagement measures, but not with felt social connection. Finally, EEG alpha power decreased and EEG delta/gamma power increased when dance was accompanied by music. Together, these data suggest that engagement with dance depends not only on what is being performed (dance/choreography/music) but also on who is performing, highlighting that dance is an inherently embodied art form that can foster social connections between people.

papers.title: Interplay of action-based prediction and top-down attention: EEG evidence for joint modulation of late perceptual processing.
papers.abstract: Voluntary action shapes our perception through sensory predictions of its consequences. These predictions are thought to inhibit perceptual processing of predicted outcomes, leading to sensory attenuation. However, some studies have reported findings that contrast with this effect, suggesting that the influence of predictions may reflect, or interact with, attentional processes. Here, we investigated the interplay of action-based prediction and top-down attention on early and late perceptual processing, with prediction and attention referring to the likelihood of a sensory event and its behavioral relevance, respectively. Electroencephalography (EEG) was recorded while participants viewed two sequential gratings. The orientation of the first was either predicted and self-generated or unpredicted and externally generated. Participants judged the tilt direction of the second grating relative to the first but responded only when the grating appeared in a task-relevant color. EEG analyses revealed no modulation of early visual potentials (N1a), but modulations at later processing stages. Specifically, the P3b exhibited reduced amplitude for predicted compared to unpredicted stimuli, but only when they were task-relevant, whereas task-relevance enhanced the P3b only for unpredicted stimuli. Interestingly, multivariate pattern analysis showed significant temporal clusters for decoding the grating's orientation exclusively for predicted and task-relevant stimuli, although decoding performance did not significantly differ between conditions. Furthermore, predicted and task-relevant stimuli elicited faster behavioral responses, with prediction-related P3b latency differences correlating with reaction-time differences. Overall, converging findings from the P3b, multivariate, time-frequency and behavioral analyses provide suggestive evidence that top-down attention and action-based prediction may jointly facilitate late perceptual and decision-related processing.

papers.title: Selective mGlu1 Receptor Activation Restores Cortical Inhibitory Tone and Improves Cognitive Performance in a Subchronic Phencyclidine NMDA Hypofunction Model.
papers.abstract: Deficits in prefrontal cortex (PFC) inhibitory transmission are thought to underlie the cognitive symptoms of schizophrenia that remain untreated by current pharmacotherapies. The metabotropic glutamate 1 (mGlu1) receptor, a subtype of the mGlu receptor family, is a promising therapeutic target because its activation enhances inhibitory transmission in the PFC through the excitation of somatostatin-expressing GABAergic (gamma-aminobutyric acidergic) interneurons (SST-INs). We used a subchronic phencyclidine (PCP) NMDA receptor antagonist mouse model, mGlu1 positive allosteric modulators (PAMs), and mice with selective deletion of mGlu1 receptors from SST-INs to examine the cell type-specific role of mGlu1 signaling in cortical inhibition and cognition. We used ex vivo whole-cell patch-clamp electrophysiology to assess inhibitory transmission in the PFC, and cognitive performance was evaluated using tests of working memory and novel object recognition. Subchronic PCP treatment impaired inhibitory synaptic transmission in the PFC, particularly onto layer V pyramidal neurons projecting to the nucleus accumbens. Pharmacological activation of mGlu1 restored inhibitory drive and reversed PCP-induced deficits in working memory and novel object recognition. Importantly, selective deletion of mGlu1 receptors from SST-INs abolished the ability of mGlu1 activation to restore cortical inhibition and cognitive function, demonstrating that these receptors are required for the therapeutic effects of mGlu1 PAMs. These findings identify SST-IN-expressed mGlu1 receptors as critical regulators of prefrontal cortical inhibition and cognition. Positive allosteric modulation of mGlu1 represents a promising therapeutic strategy for treating cognitive deficits associated with schizophrenia by restoring inhibitory circuit function.

papers.title: Mapping the Research Landscape and Global Trends: A Bibliometric Analysis of Event-related Potential in Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.abstract: There is an urgent need for objective biomarkers to facilitate early diagnosis and dynamic monitoring of Alzheimer's Disease (AD). Event-Related Potential (ERP), as a neuroelectrophysiological technique with high temporal resolution, shows great promise in addressing this demand. However, the macro-level developmental trajectory, research status, and frontier directions within this field remain to be systematically elucidated. This study employs bibliometric methods to delineate the development trends, knowledge structures, and research frontiers of ERP applications in AD, thereby offering a novel perspective for early diagnosis, dynamic monitoring, and efficacy assessment. Publications related to ERP and AD were retrieved and screened from the Web of Science Core Collection. A comprehensive quantitative and visual analysis was conducted using Microsoft Excel, CiteSpace, VOSviewer, and the bibliometrix package in R. The analysis covered publication trends, national/institutional collaboration networks, author co-occurrence, core journals, reference and keyword co-occurrence, and clustering. The number of annual publications in this field continued to grow. The United States, China, and Italy were the most productive countries, whereas the cooperation network among institutions and authors was decentralized. Keyword clustering identified six major research topics: P300/N200, Mismatch Negativity (MMN), N170, N400, Olfactory Event-Related Potential (OERP), and Electroencephalography (EEG). An analysis of the global research landscape reveals that ERP research has developed from an exploratory tool in the field of AD to an active research field of neuroscience. Journal and citation analysis indicate that the field has distinct clinical problem-driven features; keyword cluster analysis revealed six major themes corresponding to classical cognitive assessment, early sensory memory, and social cognition. Thematic analysis revealed that MMN and other ERP components that are sensitive to early abnormalities may become future research hotspots; however, the overall cooperation in this field still shows a certain degree of geographical concentration and institutional dispersion. In the future, it is necessary to build a closer international and interdisciplinary cooperation network, establish a standardized ERP evaluation scheme, and embed it throughout the entire process of early identification, staging, and monitoring of the effect of intervention in AD. This research systematically presents the current state of research, hotspots, and evolutionary trends in ERP in the field of AD. The results suggest that in the future, a closer international and interdisciplinary cooperation network and further prospective clinical validation are needed to clarify the diagnostic performance and practical application value of ERP, thereby promoting its clinical application.

papers.title: Channelrhodopsin ion selectivity determines mechanisms and efficacy of optogenetic defibrillation in human atria and ventricles.
papers.abstract: Cardiac re-entrant arrhythmias are a major cause of sudden cardiac death. Optogenetic defibrillation has emerged as a promising anti-arrhythmic strategy based on photoactivation of channelrhodopsins, yet the efficacy and potential adverse consequences of activating different classes of light-gated ion channels have not been systematically evaluated. Previous studies assessed either cation (e.g. ChR2) or anion (e.g. GtACR1) non-selective channels, both of which depolarize resting cardiomyocytes. Recently identified light-gated K+ channels (e.g. WiChR) suppress cardiomyocyte activity while maintaining the membrane potential near its resting state, but their defibrillation potential remains unexplored. We used computational simulations to compare ChR2, GtACR1 and WiChR. Single-cell simulations showed that ChR2 and GtACR1 markedly increased diastolic intracellular Ca2+ (by 42.6% and 52.6%, respectively), whereas WiChR induced only minimal changes (by 4.0%), suggesting lower pro-arrhythmogenic risk. WiChR, however, slightly increased intracellular Na+ (by 15.1% vs. 0.1% and 3.4% for ChR2 and GtACR1), consistent with the residual Na+ permeability of currently available K+-conducting channelrhodopsins. Simulations in human ventricles and atria showed that GtACR1 most effectively terminated re-entrant arrhythmias at low light intensities, whereas WiChR achieved comparable efficacy at ≥5 mW/mm2. Complementary tissue-scale simulations revealed that defibrillation occurs through depolarization within the excitable gap followed by fast Na+ channel inactivation (ChR2 and partly GtACR1), or through reduced membrane resistance at sufficiently high light intensities (large-conductance channels GtACR1 and WiChR). Overall, we demonstrate that channelrhodopsin ion selectivity is a key determinant of both optogenetic defibrillation efficacy and its underlying mechanisms. TRANSLATIONAL PERSPECTIVE: Re-entrant arrhythmias are a leading cause of sudden cardiac death. Standard therapies, including the activation of implantable cardioverter-defibrillators, carry burdens such as pain and myocardial injury. Optogenetic defibrillation has been suggested as a potentially gentler alternative, replacing high-voltage electrical shocks by photoactivation of light-gated ion channels expressed in cardiac cells. Determining which light-gated ion channel optimally balances efficacy and adverse effects on cardiac electrophysiology is critical for clinical translation. We addressed this question using computational simulations and validation experiments in zebrafish hearts. We identify ion selectivity as a key determinant of both the success rate for arrhythmia termination and the underlying mechanisms: non-selective cation- and anion-conducting channels terminate re-entry efficiently while promoting intracellular Ca2+ accumulation, a plausible substrate for pro-arrhythmic side effects that could undermine therapeutic safety. K+-conducting channels largely avoid this pro-arrhythmic risk by holding cardiomyocytes near their resting potential, albeit at the cost of requiring transmural illumination, while also causing mild Na+ accumulation attributable to residual Na+ permeability. Together, these trade-offs define clear clinical implications: K+-conducting channels may provide the safest option for optogenetic defibrillation, particularly once variants with further enhanced K+ selectivity and red-shifted activation spectra for improved operation within blood-perfused myocardium become available. KEY POINTS: We use computational simulations to compare cation non-selective (ChR2), anion non-selective (GtACR1) and K+-selective (WiChR) channelrhodopsins for optogenetic termination of re-entrant arrhythmia. Single-cardiomyocyte simulations suggest that ChR2 and GtACR1 activation can cause progressive accumulation of intracellular Ca2+, which is minimized when using WiChR. Intracellular microelectrode recordings from hearts of transgenic adult zebrafish validate the simulated voltage dynamics seen with ChR2, GtACR1 or WiChR activation. Simulations of human left ventricles and atria indicate that GtACR1 is most effective in terminating re-entrant arrhythmia at low light intensities, whereas WiChR becomes similarly effective at higher intensities. Tissue-scale simulations indicate distinct defibrillation mechanisms: excitable gap extinction by de novo action potential initiation followed by inactivation of fast Na+ channels for depolarizing channelrhodopsins (ChR2, GtACR1), and reduction in membrane resistance for the large-conductance channels (GtACR1, WiChR), effectively clamping the membrane potential at each channel's reversal potential at high light levels.

papers.title: Acute Psychosis and Dissociative Syndrome Following Binge Recreational Nitrous Oxide Use: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Recreational nitrous oxide (N2O) inhalation is increasingly prevalent among young adults, but acute psychiatric presentations following short-term binge exposure remain poorly characterized. We report a case of a female in her early 20s with no prior history of psychotic illness who developed an acute psychotic and dissociative syndrome over three days at an outdoor music festival. Her presentation followed heavy recreational N2O and 3,4-methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) exposure combined with sleep deprivation. On admission, she exhibited profound disorientation, inability to recognize close family members, polymorphic delusions, passivity phenomena, and auditory and olfactory hallucinations, requiring involuntary psychiatric hospitalization. Diagnostic workup revealed normal brain and cervical spine magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and a normal electroencephalogram (EEG) without epileptiform activity or slowing. Serum homocysteine was moderately elevated (25.2 µmol/L) alongside a low-normal vitamin B12 concentration (270 pg/mL), consistent with N2O-induced functional cobalamin deficiency; both markers normalized following parenteral vitamin B12 and oral folic acid supplementation. During inpatient stay, treatment with risperidone was followed by progressive neutropenia, which fully resolved after cross-titration to aripiprazole. She gradually regained full insight, was discharged on day 12, and remained free of psychotic symptoms at her three-week outpatient review. This case suggests that short-term binge N2O exposure, together with MDMA and sleep deprivation, may contribute to severe neuropsychiatric presentations without chronic use; it illustrates the value of measuring homocysteine rather than relying solely on serum B12 levels; and highlights potential hematological adverse effects during antipsychotic initiation.

papers.title: A hypothalamic circuit links high-fat diet exposure to anxiety-like behavior and anxiety-associated hyperphagia.
papers.abstract: Obesity and anxiety disorders are frequently comorbid, yet the neural circuit mechanisms linking metabolic and affective states remain incompletely understood. Here, in male mice exposed to long-term high-fat diet, we identify a hypothalamic circuit comprising arcuate nucleus agouti-related protein neurons and paraventricular nucleus corticotropin-releasing hormone neurons that regulates anxiety-like behavior under metabolic stress, with downstream recruitment of lateral hypothalamic area glutamatergic neurons to modulate feeding in a state-dependent manner. In vivo fiber photometry and ex vivo electrophysiology show that high-fat diet enhances activity and feeding-locked recruitment of this circuit, associated with increased anxiety-like behavior and feeding. Circuit-specific inhibition attenuates both phenotypes, whereas corticotropin-releasing hormone receptor 2 signaling in the lateral hypothalamic area selectively mediates high-fat diet-associated hyperphagia without affecting anxiety-like behavior. In this work, we show a disease-state-dependent hypothalamic circuit differentially recruited under chronic high-fat diet to coordinate anxiety-related behavior and feeding output, providing a framework for metabolic-affective interactions.

papers.title: Elucidating the relationship between protein amide I, II, and III bands and secondary structures by localized anharmonic vibrational calculations.
papers.abstract: The amide I, II, and III spectra of the insulin dimer and ubiquitin were investigated using our recently developed localized, second-order vibrational quasi-degenerate perturbation theory (VQDPT2) combined with quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics calculations. By averaging over ten snapshots from molecular dynamics trajectories, we confirmed that the computed spectra converged to a sufficient degree. Although the method has intrinsic limitations due to the neglect of vibrational coupling between neighboring amide groups, we found that the method provides a useful basis for spectral analysis of these proteins. The analysis of the averaged amide I, II, and III bands revealed that, for both proteins, the amide II and III peak positions tend to be closely associated with the coil contribution, whereas the origin of the amide I maximum is more protein dependent. The calculated amide I and III frequencies of the coil structures showed good agreement with experimental values. The spectra of each secondary structure were further subdivided according to the type of hydrogen bonding within the secondary structure. For structurally constrained α-helix and β-sheet structures, hydrogen-bond-dependent amide I frequency shifts were found to correlate with changes in the amide dihedral angles (O=C-N-H). Localized VQDPT2 enables direct interpretation of amide band shifts associated with conformational changes and provides a deeper understanding of the structural origin responsible for these band shifts.
